I have HTML5 Video Speed Control, which is great. It lets me speed up or slow down videos by the .1x increment. Even videos that do not make speed controls available can be sped up or slowed down with the extension.

I use hover zoom and chrome remote desktop a lot. Hover zoom just shows images and gifs when you hover your cursor over a link. Chrome remote desktop lets you use your phone or tablet as a mouse and keyboard for your computer even if you're not on the same wi-fi. It gives you complete access to your computer(s) when you're away from them.

I have to agree with some of the more mentioned plugins below, AdBlock and HoverZoom; I also use Magic Actions for YouTube, Momentum (good for keeping track of tasks/not slacking off), and Evernote Web Clipper.

• Pocket for saving articles and webpages for archiving and offline viewing.
  • ZenMate and HTTPS Everywhere for privacy
  • PushBullet for receiving and sending texts from my computer
  • UBlock for blocking ads
  • Smile Always for redirecting from amazon to smile.amazon, which donates a small portion of purchases to charity
  • Imagus for basically being hover zoom

I'd imagine these are all available on Firefox as well.

Google Hangouts Extension because it docks your IMs to your desktop rather than inside your Gmail tab.

Grammarly - Goes beyond spell check to grammar check. It also allows you to double-click words in your browser to have the definition pop up.

Checker Plus for Gmail - Desktop notification window pops up with the name and subject of the new mail that was received along with "Mark as Read" and "Delete" options. Being able to click "Delete" on an e-mail without switching to my Gmail tab keeps the inbox tidy and saves time.

Library Extension - When you browse books and music on Amazon, this extension automatically checks to see if your local library has the title and lets you know just above your "Add to Cart" box. Add multiple libraries if you live close to different systems like I do.
